title: First Steps in Forex
lessons/fx-1/steps/0/body: In forex you always trade one currency against another. In **EUR/USD**, the first currency (**EUR**) is the base currency and the second (**USD**) is the quote currency. A price of 1.0850 means 1 euro is worth 1.085 dollars.
lessons/fx-1/steps/1/title: What does buying a pair mean?
lessons/fx-1/steps/1/body: When you **buy** EUR/USD, you expect the **euro to get stronger against the dollar**. When you **sell**, you expect the euro to get weaker (or the dollar stronger).
lessons/fx-1/steps/1/tip: Always think about the first (base) currency: buying means you expect the base currency to rise.
lessons/fx-1/steps/2/prompt: In GBP/JPY, which one is the base currency?
lessons/fx-1/steps/2/explanation: The first currency in any pair is the base currency. Here, that's GBP.
lessons/fx-1/steps/3/prompt: You think the US dollar will get stronger against the euro. What do you do with EUR/USD?
lessons/fx-1/steps/3/explanation: If the dollar gets stronger, each euro buys fewer dollars and EUR/USD falls. So you sell.
lessons/fx-1/steps/4/statement: The forex market is open 24 hours a day, 5 days a week.
lessons/fx-1/steps/4/explanation: Forex runs nonstop from Monday morning (Asian time) to Friday evening (New York time).
lessons/fx-2/steps/0/body: A **pip** is the standard unit for measuring price changes in forex. In most pairs it's the **fourth decimal place** (0.0001). In yen pairs like USD/JPY, it's the second decimal place (0.01).
lessons/fx-2/steps/1/body: A **lot** is the unit of trade size. 1 standard lot = **100,000 units** of the base currency. On EUR/USD, with 1 lot each pip is worth about **$10**; with 0.1 lot (mini) it's $1, and with 0.01 lot (micro) it's 10 cents.
lessons/fx-2/steps/2/prompt: EUR/USD went from 1.0820 to 1.0850. How many pips did it move?
lessons/fx-2/steps/2/explanation: 1.0850 − 1.0820 = 0.0030, and every 0.0001 is one pip. So that's 30 pips.
lessons/fx-2/steps/3/prompt: You're trading 0.1 lot on EUR/USD, and price moves 20 pips in your favor. Roughly how much did you make?
lessons/fx-2/steps/3/explanation: With 0.1 lot, each pip is worth about $1. 20 pips × $1 = $20.
lessons/fx-2/steps/4/sentence: 1 standard lot equals ___ units of the base currency, and 0.01 lot is called a ___ lot.
lessons/fx-2/steps/4/explanation: Standard = 100,000 units, mini = 0.1 lot, micro = 0.01 lot.
lessons/fx-2/steps/5/explanation: Yen pairs are quoted with two decimals, so one pip equals 0.01.
lessons/fx-3/steps/0/body: **Leverage** means your broker lets you trade with more money than you have. With 1:100 leverage, $1,000 lets you open a $100,000 position. **Leverage makes profits bigger, and losses too.**
lessons/fx-3/steps/1/body: **Margin** is the part of your balance that gets locked to keep a trade open. If your losses grow and your free margin runs out, your broker issues a **margin call** and may close your trades automatically.
lessons/fx-3/steps/1/tip: Beginners should start with low leverage. High leverage is the fastest way to empty an account.
lessons/fx-3/steps/2/statement: Higher leverage makes a trade less risky.
lessons/fx-3/steps/2/explanation: Higher leverage means every small price move hits your account harder. So risk goes up, not down.
lessons/fx-3/steps/3/prompt: With 1:50 leverage and a $2,000 balance, what's the largest position you can open?
lessons/fx-3/steps/4/options/0: A broker warning that your free margin can't support your open trades
lessons/fx-3/steps/4/options/1: A broker reward for trading a lot
lessons/fx-3/steps/4/explanation: A margin call means your losses have grown so much that your free margin can no longer keep your trades open.
lessons/fx-3/steps/5/pairs/0/meaning: Trading with a multiple of your capital
lessons/fx-3/steps/5/pairs/1/meaning: Money locked to keep a trade open
lessons/fx-4/steps/0/body: Forex runs 24 hours, but it isn't equally busy all day. It has three main sessions: **Asia (Tokyo)**, **London** and **New York**. Volume and volatility are usually highest when **London and New York are open at the same time**.
lessons/fx-4/steps/1/prompt: When is the forex market usually most volatile?
lessons/fx-4/steps/1/explanation: When the two big markets, London and New York, are open together, volume and volatility peak.
lessons/fx-4/steps/2/statement: The forex market is just as active on Saturday and Sunday as on other days.
lessons/fx-4/steps/2/explanation: Forex is closed on weekends. That's why Monday's price can open with a gap.
lessons/fx-4/steps/3/prompt: Which pair is usually more active during the Asian session?
lessons/fx-4/steps/3/explanation: The Japanese yen is the main currency of the Tokyo session, so yen pairs are more active then.
lessons/fx-4/steps/4/sentence: Forex is open ___ days a week and ___ hours a day.
lessons/fx-4/steps/4/explanation: 5 days a week, 24 hours a day.
